----- Hatch is a modern, extensible Python project manager. ## Features - Standardized [build system](https://hatch.pypa.io/latest/config/build/#build-system) with reproducible builds by default - Robust [environment management](https://hatch.pypa.io/latest/environment/) with support for custom scripts and UV - Configurable [Python distribution management](https://hatch.pypa.io/latest/tutorials/python/manage/) - [Test execution](https://hatch.pypa.io/latest/tutorials/testing/overview/) with known best practices - [Static analysis](https://hatch.pypa.io/latest/config/static-analysis/) with sane defaults - Built-in Python [script runner](https://hatch.pypa.io/latest/how-to/run/python-scripts/) - Easy [publishing](https://hatch.pypa.io/latest/publish/) to PyPI or other indices - [Version](https://hatch.pypa.io/latest/version/) management - Best practice [project generation](https://hatch.pypa.io/latest/config/project-templates/) - Responsive [CLI](https://hatch.pypa.io/latest/cli/about/), ~2-3x [faster](https://github.com/pypa/hatch/actions/workflows/cli.yml) than equivalent tools See the [Why Hatch?](https://hatch.pypa.io/latest/why/) page for more information. ## Documentation The [documentation](https://hatch.pypa.io/) is made with [Material for MkDocs](https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material) and is hosted by [GitHub Pages](https://docs.github.com/en/pages). ## License Hatch is distributed under the terms of the [MIT](https://spdx.org/licenses/MIT.html) license.

payload.author: musicinmybrain
payload.body:
On MacOS: `/bin/sh: /Users/runner/Library/Application: No such file or directory`

This is because `sys.executable` is something like `/Users/runner/Library/Application Support/hatch/env/virtual/hatch/h61Cbry8/hatch-test.py3.14/bin/python3`, the construction of the test config doesn’t do shell quoting, and there is whitespace in the path.

I suppose one option would be to assume that just having the correct executable *name* from `sys.executable` suffices, and that the executable name itself doesn’t have whitespace. These aren’t necessarily bulletproof assumptions, but they are probably good enough for testing, and still an improvement over a hard-coded `python`.

Another option would be to map `sys.executable` through [`shlex.quote`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/shlex.html#shlex.quote), but this is only guaranteed to work properly for POSIXy shells.

payload.author: flying-sheep
payload.body:
Very cool! *Please* make sure to move over the regression tests from https://github.com/pypa/hatch/pull/2381 so it’s clear that these cases are fixed. We *need* to make sure that further changes don’t regress.

Comments that don’t need to be part of this PR:

I do wonder why this PR has a positive diff ratio. If it would unify the logic, wouldn’t that mean that there’s more code reuse and the diff is neutral or negative? Or is that because of the hatch-hatchling split so the logic is duplicated between both? If so – why is removing hatchling as a runtime dependency a goal if it contains logic we otherwise need to duplicate in `hatch`?

payload.author: cjames23
payload.body:
> I do wonder why this PR has a positive diff ratio. If it would unify the logic, wouldn’t that mean that there’s more code reuse and the diff is neutral or negative? Or is that because of the hatch-hatchling split so the logic is duplicated between both? If so – why is removing hatchling as a runtime dependency a goal if it contains logic we otherwise need to duplicate in `hatch`?

The code reuse is there but in order to properly centralize the logic it required an additional function in Project. 

In terms of removing hatchling as a runtime dependency as a goal, hatch as a CLI should not require hatchling the build backend in order to be used. The same is true of hatchling which already does not require hatch to be used. We are trying to have that decoupling be completed fully. Right now hatchling has to be installed even if it is not the build backend that will be used.

payload.author: cjames23
payload.body: Thanks for the contribution. The reordering (lock first, then reinstall local packages) is the right direction, but I don't think this actually fixes the reported issue. In a single-project setup with no workspace members (which is what #2372 describes),` local_dependencies_complex` won't include the root project as it's installed separately via `install_project_dev_mode()` during env creation, so `workspace_install_args` will be empty and the `if workspace_install_args:` guard means the root editable never gets reinstalled after `uv pip sync` nukes it. The fix needs to also re-install the root project itself (when skip-install is false and dev-mode is true) after applying the lock. Additionally, `get_source_install_args(self.all_dependencies_complex)` triggers metadata preparation which is wasted work under `--no-deps` since no index is consulted — the install args should just be `["--no-deps"] + workspace_install_args` directly.

payload.author: shixi-li
payload.body: Addressed both points in b3ef4022. The current local_dependencies_complex does include the root project, but the locked-sync path now makes root restoration explicit instead of depending on that collection: it adds the root whenever skip-install is false, preserves dev-mode behavior, skips the duplicate root entry, and restores workspace members separately after the lock sync. The post-lock install command is now exactly --no-deps plus the local install arguments, so it no longer prepares source metadata. The regression test explicitly asserts a single-project setup with no workspace members and verifies lock then editable root install. Validation: 34 focused lock tests passed (tests/env/test_virtual.py plus tests/cli/env/test_lock.py); test_sync_dependencies_uv passed; Ruff check/format and the targeted mypy check passed. The five upstream workflows for this fork update are currently action_required before creating checks; could a maintainer approve them when reviewing the update?
